source.title: Robo-MUTUAL: Robotic Multimodal Task Specification via Unimodal Learning
source.authors: Jianxiong Li; Zhi-Hao Wang; Jinliang Zheng; Xiao-Ai Zhou; Guan Wang; Guang-Lu Song; Yu Liu; Jing-Jing Liu; Ya-Qin Zhang; Junzhi Yu; Xianyuan Zhan

record.tranche_reason: It measures alignment between paired visual and language task representations and compares ways to reduce their modality gap, using cosine similarity and qualitative visualizations rather than testing scale across independently trained models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream robot-policy transfer between visual and textual prompts, but those task-success results do not directly measure representation similarity or one model's representations mapped onto another's. The numerical values in the alignment and ablation figures are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as motivation and uses jointly, contrastively trained vision-language encoders (CLIP, LIV, DecisionNCE) as a tool for robot policies. These encoders are trained on purpose to align images and text, so their alignment is not convergence between independently trained models. No version is tested. The paper's main evidence is robot task success, and its encoder-alignment and gap-reduction results concern its own engineered pipeline. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that unimodal-prompt training, combined with a broadly pretrained robotic multimodal encoder and training-free gap reduction, yields multimodal task specification. They list limits: only language and image modalities, and the need for better encoders and gap-reduction methods.
record.recipe_differences: This is a robotics application that retrains a visual encoder on robot-relevant data, keeps the CLIP language encoder frozen, and reduces the modality gap by centralizing or deleting dimensions; it does not reproduce the original scale-alignment method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper compares centralize with delete, and cosine-similarity noise with Gaussian noise at different standard deviations; it reports comparable performance for the two collapse methods and instability of Gaussian noise across standard deviations. It also varies the cosine-similarity noise threshold α.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastively trained vision-language encoders (CLIP, LIV, DecisionNCE) align matched robot visual goals and instructions poorly. Retraining the visual encoder on broader robot data against frozen CLIP text improves alignment, but matched-pair cosine is only about 0.2, and a modality gap separates the modalities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive multimodal encoders retain a modality gap, and their in-domain alignment depends on training-data coverage.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting each modality's mean, or deleting the dimension with the largest mean difference, mostly collapses matched visual and text embeddings together (t-SNE).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The modality gap in contrastive encoders is concentrated in a few dimensions or a constant offset and is removable post hoc.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
record.problems: The representation-alignment figures provide no numerical values in the text. The alignment comparison retrains the visual encoder while keeping the language encoder fixed, so it does not test improvement of both models. The reported task evaluations are downstream policy outcomes, not direct measures of representational similarity.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream simulation and real-robot task-success results, including the ablation plots in Figs. 7–9, are not recorded as rows because they measure policy success rather than representation similarity or cross-model representation mapping.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models across scale or capability.
No independently trained vision and language models; the encoders are contrastively aligned by design, and there is no capability sweep of both models.
No seed comparison of features or subspaces.
No mapping between different models' representations; centralization is applied within one encoder's two modalities.
No comparison of similarity metrics or of input dependence.
No measurement of alignment level or plateau between independent models, and no causal attribution.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' should be T4. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis is cited only as motivation. Cross-modal alignment here is an engineered contrastive objective plus post-hoc collapse, so it does not bear on emergent convergence. The only number in the text is the matched-pair cosine of about 0.2 in Fig 3(d).

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of alignment across independently trained models as they scale.

The language encoder is frozen; the study does not test whether alignment rises as both models improve, nor whether it rises with model scale or across independently trained vision and language models.
No comparison across random seeds or shared-feature/subspace analysis.
The study aligns visual and language task prompts for robot policies; it does not map one model's representations onto another's using the listed methods.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.
It does not compare similarity metrics, neighbourhood settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution representation similarity. It does compare gap-reduction and corruption methods.

It reports a remaining modality gap and compares encoders trained on different data, but does not establish a plateau or isolate shared data/objectives as the cause instead of a common model of reality.

rows.subject: CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity of paired visual goals and language instructions.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of visual and language goal representations
rows.note: The text says the evaluated encoders fail to align matched goals well; it does not give a numerical similarity.
rows.check: CLIP is trained with a contrastive objective to align images and text. Its matched-pair cosine similarity on robot goals measures engineered alignment and domain fit, not convergence of independently trained models with capability. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: LIV
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity of paired visual goals and language instructions.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of visual and language goal representations
rows.note: The text says the evaluated encoders fail to align matched goals well; it does not give a numerical similarity.
rows.check: Same issue as R1: LIV is a contrastive vision-language encoder, so it is not a test of V2 or V7. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: DecisionNCE
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity of paired visual goals and language instructions.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of visual and language goal representations
rows.note: The text says the evaluated encoders fail to align matched goals well; it does not give a numerical similarity.
rows.check: Same issue as R1: DecisionNCE is a contrastive vision-language encoder. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: DecisionNCE (Robo-MUTUAL)
rows.stage_stated: retrained visual encoder; language encoder frozen
rows.operation_detail: Retrained the visual encoder on Open-X, DROID, and EPICK-KITCHEN data; retained the pretrained CLIP language encoder, then measured matched-pair cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of visual and language goal representations
rows.baseline: DecisionNCE, CLIP, and LIV shown as comparisons
rows.value: figure only; text says matched-pair similarity is high and alignment is strong
rows.note: Alignment is reported as strong after broader-data visual-encoder training, but no numerical value is given and the language encoder is fixed.
rows.check: This is the study's own retrained encoder: a contrastive visual encoder trained against a frozen CLIP text encoder. Better alignment from more data under an alignment objective is induced by training. Text says matched pairs average about 0.2 cosine before corruption (Fig 3(d)).

rows.subject: DecisionNCE (Robo-MUTUAL)
rows.operation_detail: Visualized matched visual and language representations before gap reduction.
rows.measure: Separation of matched visual and language representations by modality
rows.value: figure only; text describes the modalities as initially separate with a large gap
rows.note: The text explicitly reports a remaining modality gap in the pretrained representation space.
rows.check: A modality gap inside one contrastive encoder (t-SNE only) is not V7's partial convergence between independent models.

rows.subject: DecisionNCE (Robo-MUTUAL)
rows.operation_detail: Centralized each modality's representations by subtracting its estimated mean, then visualized matched pairs.
rows.measure: Clustering of matched visual and language representations
rows.value: figure only; text says centralizing can mostly bridge the gap and collapse the representations together
rows.note: Centralize is the method used for the paper's main results.
rows.check: This row reports the study's own gap-reduction method (centralize), a post-hoc manipulation. It should not be a row bearing on convergence. Evidence is t-SNE only.

rows.subject: DecisionNCE (Robo-MUTUAL)
rows.operation_detail: Deleted the embedding dimension with the largest difference between modality means, then visualized matched pairs.
rows.measure: Clustering of matched visual and language representations
rows.value: figure only; text says deleting dimensions can mostly bridge the gap and collapse the representations together
rows.note: The paper says centralize and delete both effectively cluster matched pairs.
rows.check: Same as R6, for the delete method, which is also the study's own manipulation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DecisionNCE (Robo-MUTUAL), matched visual and language goals after broader-data visual-encoder training
reader_labels.reason: The reported cosine-similarity heatmap and text indicate strong alignment for matched pairs, though no numeric values are supplied and only the visual encoder was retrained (R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Pretrained representations before gap reduction and representations after centralize or delete
reader_labels.reason: A modality gap remains before reduction; the two reduction methods are described as mostly bridging it rather than establishing complete convergence (R5–R7).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Evaluated pretrained encoders and Robo-MUTUAL representations before gap reduction
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the standard encoders do not align matched goals well and that a substantial modality gap remains even after Robo-MUTUAL pretraining (R1–R5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: After centralize or delete gap reduction
reader_labels.reason: The reported methods mostly bridge the gap and bring matched modalities together, so the remaining gap is not shown to be unavoidable (R6–R7).
